MCPHealthResponse.description:
Response for GET /pipeline/mcp/health (epic-026 Task-09).

Status mapping:
  * ``healthy``     — last probe returned ACK and ≥1 tool is registered.
  * ``degraded``    — soft-disable active (1-2 consecutive probe failures)
                      or MCP server answered partially.
  * ``unavailable`` — MCP disabled in config, or ≥3 consecutive probe
                      failures (``MCP_PROBE_FAIL_ALERT_THRESHOLD`` in
                      :mod:`makeit_pipeline.mcp_health_probe`).

``last_probe`` is an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (timezone-aware). When the
endpoint reports the config-disabled case without running a probe the
field still carries the current time so dashboards can reason about
freshness uniformly.
MCPHealthResponse.title: MCPHealthResponse

ReplayJobStatus.description:
Response for GET /pipeline/replay/{job_id}.

Populated progressively as the background task runs. While ``status =
running`` only ``job_id`` / ``started_at`` are guaranteed — the numeric
fields (``regressions_count`` / ``total`` / ``regression_rate``) and
``report_path`` arrive on ``completed``.  On ``failed`` the ``error``
field carries a sanitized message suitable for user display (internal
paths / stack traces are logged but not returned).

ReplayRequest.description:
Request body for POST /pipeline/replay.

Mirrors the CLI ``makeit-pipeline replay`` flags so dashboard operators
can trigger the same offline regression harness without shelling in.
Pydantic enforces the ``1 <= sample <= 50`` cap at the API boundary so a
malicious/confused caller cannot spend unbounded LLM budget (epic-030
risk section — replay cost is O(sample * n_samples_per_issue)).

get.description:
Unified health of pipeline + auditor + SSH tunnel.

Replaces the three-curl operator workflow from CLAUDE.md §Remote
Access. Dashboard polls this every ~30s and renders a coloured
dot per service. All three checks run in parallel so total
response time is bounded by the slowest individual check
(currently ``auditor`` at 5 s).

Each sub-check converts any failure mode — timeout, connection
refused, non-2xx — into ``status: "down"`` rather than bubbling
up. We never want this endpoint to 500; dashboards interpret a
missing response the same way as "pipeline is itself down",
which would be misleading when only auditor / tunnel are out.

schema.title: Response Health All Health All Get

get.description:
Return the full :class:`IssueContext` JSON for ``{repo}#{issue_number}``.

``repo`` is captured via ``{repo:path}`` so values containing a
forward slash (e.g. ``Sergio1990-1/makeit-pipeline``) route
correctly.  The captured value is validated against a strict
``owner/name`` pattern before being passed to the store to
prevent path-traversal attacks via ``..`` segments.

Returns 404 when no context is stored.  The detail message
contains only the requested ``repo`` / ``issue_number`` — no
internal paths — so a probe cannot use the response to map the
contexts directory layout.

schema.title: Response Get Issue Context Issue  Repo   Issue Number  Context Get

get.description:
Return merges that bypassed branch protection via ``--admin``.

Reads ``metrics.jsonl`` and returns every record with
``admin_bypassed=true`` (and ``result='merged'``) so the dashboard
can flag them for post-hoc human review.

Parameters
----------
since:
    Optional ISO-8601 timestamp.  Records with ``ts >= since`` are
    included; everything older is dropped.  Invalid input yields
    ``HTTP 400`` so the dashboard can render a clear error rather
    than silently returning the full history.

Behaviour notes
---------------
- Missing ``metrics.jsonl`` (fresh install / never ran) → empty list,
  *not* a 5xx.  The dashboard must be able to render this lane on
  day-1 even before any metric has been logged.
- Malformed JSON lines are skipped (mirrors
  ``_compute_success_rate_by_complexity``); we never let a single
  bad record break the response.
- The endpoint reads ``metrics.jsonl`` directly — no path traversal
  surface (``since`` is parsed as a datetime and never used as a
  path component).

schema.title: Response List Admin Bypass Merges Pipeline Admin Bypass Merges Get

get.description:
Return the last *lines* lines of a whitelisted LaunchAgent log.

Unlike ``/pipeline/logs/{filename}`` which serves per-issue JSONL
agent logs, this endpoint exposes the stdout/stderr captured by
the Mac-hosted services (pipeline API, auditor API) so dashboard
users don't need SSH to see recent runtime output.

Registered before ``/pipeline/logs/{filename}`` because FastAPI
routes by insertion order; the parametric route would otherwise
capture ``tail`` as a filename and shadow this handler.

Parameters
----------
service:
    One of ``pipeline`` / ``auditor`` (whitelist).  Any other
    value yields 400 — no arbitrary path access.
lines:
    How many tail lines to return.  Clamped to ``1 <= lines <= 1000``
    to bound memory / response size.

get.description:
Return the MCP server health (epic-026 Task-09).

Non-blocking (INV-E26-3): reads ``pipeline_state.mcp_health_snapshot``
which the pipeline populates whenever it runs an MCP health probe
during a batch.  If no snapshot is cached yet (fresh process /
pipeline not running) we fall back to introspecting the registered
FastMCP instance synchronously — listing tools is an in-process dict
lookup, so it never shells out.

Status mapping:
  * ``unavailable`` — MCP disabled in config, OR ≥3 consecutive probe
    failures (``_MCP_UNAVAILABLE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD``),
    OR cached snapshot reports no tools.
  * ``degraded`` — soft-disable active / 1-2 consecutive probe
    failures / probe partially succeeded.
  * ``healthy`` — last probe returned ACK and ≥1 tool registered.

post.description:
Kick off a replay-harness job and return its ``job_id``.

The heavy lifting (collecting ``ReplayInput``s, running the harness,
rendering the MD report) is scheduled as an ``asyncio`` task so this
handler returns immediately with ``202 Accepted``.  Poll
:func:`get_replay` with the returned ``job_id`` for status /
regression numbers / report path.

``sample`` > 50 / ``sample`` < 1 / ``n_samples_per_issue`` < 1 are all
rejected by Pydantic (422) before this handler runs — we don't
re-validate here.

Side effect: when ``len(replay_jobs) >= MAX_REPLAY_JOBS``, oldest
terminal (completed/failed) entries are evicted by ``started_at`` to
bound memory growth on long-lived LaunchAgent deployments.

schema.title: Response Start Replay Pipeline Replay Post

delete.description:
Delete a terminal replay job from the in-memory store.

Returns:
    * ``200 {"deleted": true, "job_id": ...}`` — record removed.
    * ``404`` — no such job (never started, or already evicted/deleted).
    * ``409`` — job is still ``running`` (symmetric with
      ``/research/{job_id}`` / ``/discovery/{job_id}`` semantics: we
      don't permit deleting an in-flight record because the background
      worker still mutates it and ``_replay_tasks`` still tracks it).

Note: this is an in-memory delete; there is no job_dir on disk to
remove (report files live under ``~/.makeit-pipeline/reports/`` and
are intentionally preserved for audit — matching the module docstring
above).

schema.title: Response Delete Replay Pipeline Replay  Job Id  Delete

post.description:
Regenerate a BRIEF that a speaker merge marked stale.

Only valid for a job whose output_mode is "brief", status is
"done", and whose BRIEF is actually flagged stale (see
``is_brief_stale`` / ``apply_speaker_merge``) — any other state is a
409 (running, wrong output_mode, not done, or not stale — a
redundant call is rejected rather than treated as a silent no-op,
matching /transcript/continue's existing "wrong state" convention).
Missing manifest/stt artifacts is a 422, matching /continue's
missing-upload-file guard.

Dispatches the same ``_process_transcript_job(..., is_resume=True)``
worker used by fresh uploads and /continue. No audio is
re-transcribed: apply_speaker_merge already rolled this job's
manifest checkpoint back to ``[intake, stt]`` when it set the stale
flag, so the resume path's ``stt_already_done`` guard skips
straight to numeric_facts/enrichment/structuring/synthesis, which
reprocess from the corrected transcript. The stale flag itself is
only cleared once synthesis actually succeeds (see
``process_transcript``'s stage loop) — the old BRIEF.md is left on
disk untouched in the meantime, but job status flips to "queued"
immediately so status/result endpoints don't present it as current
mid-regeneration.

get.description:
List speakers detected in a job's STT output for human review.

Reads directly from enriched_stt.json on disk (not job-dict memory)
so it works identically for a freshly-processed job and one
restored after a restart. Takes the same per-job resume lock as
merge/continue so it never reads artifacts mid-write (_save_artifact
isn't an atomic write).

post.description:
Merge/rename one or more speakers and rebuild normalized_transcript.md.

Idempotent — repeating an identical request is a no-op the second
time. If this job's BRIEF was already generated, its manifest
checkpoint is rolled back to stt and ``brief_stale=True`` is
returned so callers don't mistake the existing BRIEF for current
(see ``apply_speaker_merge`` for the full rationale).

The done/running check is re-verified *after* acquiring the resume
lock, not before — a concurrent ``/transcript/continue/{job_id}``
call can flip status to "queued" and dispatch its own background
task in the window between an earlier check and this lock being
acquired. Re-checking inside the lock (mirroring /continue's own
pattern) closes that window instead of racing the newly-dispatched
background task's writes to the same artifact files.
